  "notes": "The paper is a high-quality faithful compression of IMF Country Report No. 22/334 (Mexico 2022 Article IV). It preserves the concrete mechanisms, figures, dates, and contested material needed to reason about each Chapter 5B question: fiscal stance/headline deficit (3.8% GDP 2022; 4.1% 2023 projection), debt (~56% GDP), FEIP stabilization fund depletion (<0.1% of GDP, MEX$25bn end-June 2022, proposed MEX$20–30bn replenishment), fuel-subsidy mechanism (1.4% GDP cost, 2pp inflation reduction, distributional incidence), Banxico's tightening path (25→50→75 bp hikes, 9.25% rate, ~6pp above Fed), FSAP findings (CAR 19%, NPL 2.3%, ROE 17.4%), AML/CFT and beneficial-ownership status, subcontracting-law transition (87%/70% reductions in manufacturing/retail), 2021 pension reform parameters (6.5–10%→15% by 2030, 25→15 years minimum with phased return to 20 by 2031), 2013 energy-reform reversal and the 2022 electricity law, tax-reform gap (0.2% GDP 2023 rising to 1.3% by 2027), recommended VAT/PIT/property/carbon-tax options, U.S.-cycle correlation (1.5x elasticity in 2010s), remittance buffers (~4% GDP 2021), and the principal-risk matrix with quantified likelihoods. Locators are preserved as paragraph/table/figure references (e.g., ¶6 p.6; ¶23 p.15; Box 1 p.9; Annex X pp.79–83; Annex VI pp.69–71; Annex XIII pp.87–88; Annex XI p.84). Authorities' disagreements (fuel subsidy, anti-inflation package, energy policy, AML/CFT, labor informality, fiscal framework, inflation outlook, contingent credit lines) are explicitly recorded with original phrasing where it matters. Source limitations (no political-economy detail on electoral mandate, military role beyond ¶58 mention, agency autonomy dispute, or specific patronage/procurement episodes) are honestly flagged in §X. No consequential factual distortions, mis-attributions, or back-cover summarizing were detected; no episodes whose loss would force the judge to reopen the original for ordinary reasoning about 5B claims."
